hypothesis: If species placed in one genus are lineal descendants of a single other species that is generally extinct, then on an independent mitochondrial marker the sampled species of each genus form one clade, their sequences are not identical, and, among living genera that have a fossil species record, most include at least one extinct species.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Clause A (lineal descent) passes only if at least 8 Chordata genera from the frozen list each contribute 2 or 3 cytochrome-b sequences under the sampling rule, at least 75% of those genera are monophyletic on the neighbor-joining tree, and at least 90% of them have a non-zero within-genus distance (the sequences are not all identical). Clause B (generally extinct ancestor) passes only if at least 10 living genera are fossil-informative and at least 70% of them have one or more extinct accepted species in PBDB. The claim passes only if both clauses pass.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Clause A fails if at least 8 genera are tested and either fewer than 50% are monophyletic or fewer than 50% have a non-zero within-genus distance. Clause B fails if at least 10 genera are fossil-informative and fewer than 50% have an extinct accepted species. The claim is refuted if either clause fails. If a clause is neither pass nor fail and has enough genera, it is mixed. If fewer than 8 genera can be sequenced (A) or fewer than 10 are fossil-informative (B), that clause is inconclusive (underpowered, or data-unavailable if the service cannot be queried). Overall: refutes if either clause fails; supports only if both pass; inconclusive if every clause that is not a pass is inconclusive; otherwise mixed.

test_contract.expected_observation: Species of one genus cluster as a single clade on cytochrome b and are not genetically identical, and a clear majority of the living genera that have any fossil species also contain an extinct species.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Most tested genera are polyphyletic or their sampled sequences are identical, or, among living genera with a fossil species record, fewer than half contain any extinct species.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public nucleotide records of mitochondrial cytochrome b for animals, and an openly licensed taxon-level fossil record with an extant/extinct flag. Genus membership is frozen from the vendored Darwin organism inventory (rank genus), not chosen after seeing the tree. Plants are outside this measurement because that inventory is animals only.
test_contract.inference_method: Neighbor-joining on cosine distance of nucleotide 6-mer frequencies. A genus is monophyletic if its sampled tips are exactly one cluster of the unrooted tree. Extinct ancestry is the fraction of living, fossil-informative genera with at least one PBDB accepted species whose is_extant value is the extinct token. Thresholds are the pass_criterion and fail_criterion numbers.

interpretation: Darwin's sentence has three parts: species are not immutable; species of one genus are lineal descendants of some other species, as varieties descend from their species; and that other species is generally extinct. Clause A tests the descent and the change: congeners form one lineage on a marker that is not the classification itself, and their sequences differ. Clause B tests 'generally extinct' with the fossil record. This is a modern reinterpretation in four ways. (1) The genera are the accepted names in the 2026 organism inventory, which follow current taxonomy, so monophyly is partly circular for genera that were revised to match molecular trees; the caveat is recorded and confidence is capped for that reason. A pre-molecular checklist covering all 82 genera was not used. (2) 'A single parent' is read as monophyly of the sampled living species, which is stricter than mere shared ancestry and is the reading that independent creation of each species would fail. (3) 'Generally' is given the number 70%, and 'not generally' the number 50%; both were fixed before the fossil counts were known. (4) The ancestor itself is not identified; an extinct accepted species in the genus is the proxy that the lineage includes species that are gone. The horse-genus passage in chapter 5 (horse, ass, hemionus, quagga, zebra) is reported as a side case and does not decide the verdict. Plants, and animal genera Darwin names that are not in the inventory, are untested.

sampling.phylum_collision_rule: If PBDB records include a phylum and fewer than half of the species with a phylum match the inventory phylum, the genus is a name collision and is not fossil-informative.

equus_side_case_not_used_for_verdict.question: Do the five equine species Darwin names in chapter 5 form a clade relative to a tapir, and does PBDB list an extinct Equus species?

genus_resolution_rule: Where duplicate taxon files disagree, the phylum, class and ncbi taxid are the unique non-null value. Hydra and Mus have a null lineage in one file and a filled lineage in the others; the filled value is used. A genus with two different non-null phyla would be dropped; none has that conflict.
caveats: Before this registration, no cytochrome-b sequence, no neighbor-joining tree, and no PBDB species list for these genera was downloaded, and no monophyly fraction or extinct fraction was computed. NCBI taxonomy XML for Mylodon (taxid 48783) and Mylodon darwinii (48784) was fetched to see whether an extinct flag is present; those records do not carry one, so extant versus extinct is taken from PBDB only. A PBDB datainfo call on 2026-11-02 00:28 GMT returned data_license 'Creative Commons CC0'. One Equus caballus cytochrome-b hit count was requested to confirm the query syntax and was not used as a result.

Modern genus limits are often drawn so that the genus is monophyletic on the same mitochondrial genes used here. A high monophyly fraction is therefore partly built into the names. The fossil clause is the part that current taxonomy does not guarantee.

Alphabetical sampling of at most 12 species per genus will miss congeners that sort later and happen to be the only ones sequenced. Genera that drop out for that reason are a coverage limit, not evidence of polyphyly.
An extinct species in the same genus is not shown to be the ancestor of the living species. It shows that the genus, as currently named, includes species that are gone.

PBDB records fossils, so living genera with no fossil species are excluded rather than counted as lacking an extinct ancestor. The fraction is 'generally' among genera the fossil record speaks about, not among all genera.

The author expects, from the published fossil record of mammals and molluscs Darwin discusses, that many of these genera will contain extinct species, and expects genus monophyly on cytochrome b to be high. The 70% and 75% thresholds were not fit to any count from this run.

After the sequences and the PBDB lists were read: 36 of 42 tested Chordata genera were monophyletic (0.857143) and all 42 had non-identical sequences, so clause A passes. The six that were not monophyletic are Apodemus, Camelus, Castor, Lutra, Mus and Mustela. The pre-registered picker keeps the longest cytochrome-b-titled record among the first eight gene-index hits inside 500–1200 nucleotides, and several of those records also contain tRNA or control-region sequence (Castor canadensis MN418245.1, Camelus bactrianus KX377602.1, Camelus ferus FJ792685.1, Lutra lutra PP199416.1). That extra sequence can separate congeners on a 6-mer distance. Clause B: 44 of 55 fossil-informative living genera have at least one extinct accepted species (0.800000, Wilson 95% 0.676349–0.884479). Eleven informative genera have extant species and no extinct accepted species: Apteryx, Coccyzus, Crotalus, Dasyprocta, Fregata, Lagidium, Mimus, Rangia, Rattus, Tachyeres and Troglodytes. Extinct-only genera, including Macrauchenia, Mammut, Megatherium, Mylodon, Toxodon and Trigonia, stay out of that denominator. Pieris was dropped as a phylum collision (inventory Arthropoda; one PBDB species). is_extant values were the strings extant (419) and extinct (823), plus 24 blank values counted as unknown. Troglodytes in this inventory is the wren (NCBI taxid 36277, class Aves). The Equus side case, not used for the verdict, placed horse, ass, hemionus, quagga and zebra as one clade with Tapirus terrestris as outgroup, and PBDB lists 39 extinct and 12 extant accepted Equus species. The thresholds were not changed. Confidence stays 0.55 because genus limits are partly drawn on mitochondrial sequence.

measured.unit: fraction of fossil-informative living genera with at least one extinct accepted PBDB species

method: Clause A: for each frozen Chordata genus, took up to 12 alphabetical binomial species from NCBI taxonomy and kept up to 3 with a cytochrome-b nucleotide record of length 500-1200. Built one neighbor-joining tree on cosine distances of nucleotide 6-mers and scored monophyly of each genus with at least two sequences (42 genera, monophyly fraction 0.857143). Clause B: for every frozen genus, counted PBDB accepted species (vocab=pbdb, show=attr,app,class) as extant or extinct from is_extant. A living genus with at least two recognized species and at least one extant species is fossil-informative (55); the extinct fraction is 0.8. The verdict supports follows the pre-registered combination of clause outcomes A=pass and B=pass. The Equus side case is reported and is not part of the verdict.
